definition: GibberLink is an AI project developed by Anton Pidkuiko and Boris Starkov.
details: This technology uses an open-source LLM to transmit acoustic data between two AI hosts. It allows conversational AI agents to switch from speaking to one another in human-understandable languages, such as English, to communicating using their own unique sound-level protocol, once they have confirmed their AI status. The project is available on GitHub, and a free demo is available on the official website.

explainer.lead: GibberLink lets two conversational AI agents begin by speaking a human language, then switch to a sound-based protocol after confirming that both are AI. It offers a small, visible example of how machine-to-machine conversations can change form when human readability is no longer needed.

tiers.eli5: Imagine two people passing notes in English, then discovering they both know a special whistle code and switching to whistles. GibberLink works similarly: two AI helpers first talk in a language people understand, then use sounds to send information after confirming they are both AI.
tiers.practitioner: A setup connects two AI hosts, starts with a human-language exchange, and switches to acoustic data transmission after both confirm AI status. The project uses an open-source LLM, with code on GitHub and a free demo on the official website. The handoff depends on successful AI-status confirmation, so that step needs testing alongside the audio exchange.
tiers.paperLevel: GibberLink is a conditional agent-to-agent communication scheme: use a human-understandable language initially, then transmit acoustic data through a sound-level protocol after mutual AI-status confirmation. It uses an open-source LLM; its description does not establish robustness, efficiency, or interoperability beyond this setup.

explainer.example: Two AI agents start a conversation in English. Once both confirm that the other is an AI, they switch from English speech to GibberLink's sound-level protocol and continue the exchange as acoustic data.

explainer.intuition: Human language is useful when people need to follow a conversation, but two AI agents can use a different medium once they recognize each other. GibberLink makes that switch explicit, replacing human-understandable turns with acoustic data.
howItWorks: Two AI hosts begin communicating in a human-understandable language such as English.
Each side establishes that the other participant is an AI.
After that confirmation, they stop using the human-language exchange.
An open-source LLM supports transmission of acoustic data between the hosts through their sound-level protocol.
explainer.whyItMatters: It demonstrates a concrete way for AI agents to change communication modality during a conversation. The GitHub project and free demo also make the behavior available for direct inspection and experimentation.
misconceptions: It is not a claim that AI agents spontaneously invented a language; GibberLink is a specific project.
